This is github.com/robinson/gos7 at commit c54e650665ba (2026-09-24, the latest
on master; the module has no tagged releases) under BSD-3-Clause (LICENSE in
this directory), minus its tests and its documentation PDFs, with one change.
Flow's go.mod replaces the module with this directory.

Why: Send in tcpclient.go writes a raw line to Go's global logger every time
the first read of a reply fails:

    log.Printf("%T %+v", err, err)

On every S7 timeout that put "*net.OpError read tcp ...: i/o timeout" on
stderr. Nobody can do anything with that line. The node already hands the flow
an error that says what happened and what to check on the CPU. The handler's
Logger field is the library's own switch for its logging, and this line
ignores it. I won't point the global logger at the bin to hide it, because that
would swallow every other library's output too, and a wrapper around the
transport would break the type assertions the library makes on its own handler
types in client.go and multi.go. So the copy is the fix.

Change, and only this:
  tcpclient.go  line 154: log.Printf("%T %+v", err, err) is now
                mb.logf("%T %+v", err, err). Same text, but it goes to the
                handler's Logger, which Flow leaves nil, so nothing is written.
                Anyone who sets Logger still sees it, as they see every other
                line the library logs.

Every other byte of every other file is upstream's. A future upgrade is a diff
of this one line. The proof is TestS7TimeoutDoesNotWriteToTheGlobalLogger in
internal/nodes/s7_test.go: it points a node at a listener that never answers,
captures the global logger, and fails if anything lands in it.

Dropping it: when upstream stops writing that line (open issue 78 asks for a
way to turn the library's logging off; no fix is merged, checked 2026-10-19),
delete this directory, delete the replace line in go.mod, take the new commit
with go get, remove the COPY third_party line from the Dockerfile, remove the
gos7 section from NOTICE, and keep TestS7TimeoutDoesNotWriteToTheGlobalLogger:
it is what proves the new release is quiet. Check with:
gh issue view 78 -R robinson/gos7
